To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) N-GCN is the first model to train multiple instances of GCN over random walks to achieve state-of-the-art results in node classification; 2) N-GCN generalizes to other semi-supervised methods such as Graph-SAGE; 3) N-GCN achieves the best results on adversarially perturbed graphs; and 4) N-GCN outperforms all other models on the challenging PPI dataset.

We propose a new architecture, Network of Graph Convolution Networks (N-GCNs), which trains multiple instances of the GCN architecture over node pairs discovered in random walks, learns an aggregation of the instance predictions, and achieves state-of-the art performance on the challenging Cora, Citseeer, Pubmed and PPI node classification tasks.

we propose a model that combines the benefits of GCNs with random walk-based node embedding methods, and demonstrate the benefits of this approach through extensive experimentation on a variety of tasks.

random walks are a powerful tool for improving the performance of GCNs on node classification tasks, and that the proposed model is a promising starting point for future work in this direction.
